scope: Proposition 5.2 (Dilation in the symmetry algebra) of the manuscript “Entropy equality and local symmetry in negative curvature” (preprints/Entropy-equality-and-local-symmetry-in-negative-curvature-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 339 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8658ab8209a8aa0c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 28. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In the coordinates of Lemma 5.1, H = −T + θ0(D), ZH = D − T∂τ (5.7) belongs to k ⊂ h. The operator ad H on formal Hamiltonians is D and is semisimple on every finite Taylor quotient, with real weights. Every closed ad H-invariant linear subspace admits the continuous projections onto each individual weight. On a finite-dimensional continuous invariant subquotient, weight-zero vectors have weight-zero lifts. Moreover h0 ⊂ k, and ξ vanishes on every nonzero weight space.
